messages:
alex: Heads-up: I'm prototyping a compaction safepoint to do GPU<->host defrag during low-load. Want a quick sanity check on tradeoffs: stop-the-world vs incremental slices, mmap remap vs copy, and behavior for pinned KV-cache pages.

jordan: Nice. Do you mean a coordinated epoch where we quiesce alloc/free paths for a tenant?

alex: Yeah. Rough idea: mark an epoch, drain transient allocs, run a bounded compaction pass that either remaps free holes (if contiguous) or copies live ranges out to new backing and frees old extents. Then exit epoch.

linh: Remap is attractive for perf but risky with mmap granularity + CUDA pinning. If page size mismatch or GPU pinned ranges exist, remap may not be possible.

maria: Also need to consider eviction/offsload races. If evictor kicks while compaction is mid-copy we can end up double-free or resurrecting stale handles. We need an ownership transfer protocol.

alex: Agreed. Thinking of a three-state transition for pages: LIVE -> MOVING -> MOVED. During MOVING, readers must consult an indirection table. Post-move, update mappings and clear MOVING.

sam: Indirection table adds a lookup per access — could blow tail latency on small token requests. Can we limit MOVING windows or use hardware-assisted remap where possible?

alex: Plan: prefer remap when possible (no pin, aligned), fall back to copy+swap for others. Keep MOVING windows tiny (batch size cap + yield points). Also expose per-tenant max-latency SLO to throttle compaction intensity.

jordan: What about pinned KV-cache pages? We can't copy while pinned by CUDA. Option: defer those pages, collect them into a later pass, or try coordinated unpin/unmap using CUDA APIs (risky).

maria: Defer makes sense. But deferred set can fragment persistent allocation space. Might need a background coalesce that runs only when tenant underutilized.

alex: Here's rough pseudo for the compaction loop:```c
// compact safepoint epoch
compact_enter(epoch);
for (batch : choose_victims(max_batch)) {
  prepare_batch(batch);
  if (can_remap(batch)) remap_batch(batch);
  else copy_and_swap(batch);
  yield_to_inflight(); // let RPCs drain
}
compact_exit(epoch);
```

linh: That yield_to_inflight() is key. We need integration with in-flight request tracking (KV cache, running sequences) so we don't break active handles. Also add a timeout fallback to abort batch and rollback if stuck.

sam: Rollback complexity scares me. Maybe we should design for idempotent swaps: create new extents, publish them only after fully valid, then atomically flip pointer. If publish fails, old mapping still valid.

maria: Atomic flip works but requires the indirection table to already be consulted by readers. That's the perf tradeoff Sam called out. Can we limit indirection table checks to the first N tokens of a request? Probably not safe.

alex: Thoughts on observability? I want compact metrics: batches/sec, bytes_moved, avg_move_latency, blocked_pinned_pages, rollback_count. Ops console should show active epochs by tenant.

ops-bot: deploy-check: compact-safepoint-proto branch passes CI, bench job still running (ETA ~12m).

jordan: One more: interaction with mmap granularity and huge pages. If tenant uses 2MB hugepages, remap semantics change. We need to annotate hugepage-backed extents and opt-out of remap, or treat at coarser granularity.

linh: Agreed. Add a policy: never remap across hugepage boundaries; fallback to copy. Also add a compact policy per-alloc-class (tiny, small, large) so we don't try to coalesce tiny objs at hugepage pace.

maria: For rollout: start with read-only compaction (metrics only), then opt-in per-tenant with canary, with auto-throttle and a kill-switch. Add a regression test: long-running chat session + compaction during tail to ensure latency SLA holds.

alex: Great. I'll iterate the prototype with: safe epoch, indirection table + atomic publish, batch cap + yield, pinned-page deferral, hugepage awareness, and observability. Will post a short RFC follow-up with diagrams and API sketches.

sam: :thumbsup: Please add a checklist for failure modes (powerloss mid-copy, kernel OOM, process crash) and how we recover.

alex: Will do. Thanks all.
